The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T04:19:25Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T04:19:49Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-11T04:13:00Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T04:21:37Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 8 minutes 37 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 1 minute 51 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T04:21:37Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 30.8% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 40.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 29.8% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 1% {series_before} before it began, 30.833333333333335% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 40.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 5,890.09 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T04:19:46Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T04:20:00Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T04:20:00Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T04:20:06Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 04:19:25 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T04:20:11Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 361 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T04:20:12Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 04:13 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T04:20:12Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T04:20:13Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 11 04:14 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T04:20:15Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T04:20:15Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T04:20:15Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes 25 {T11.3} seconds before 04:19:25 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T04:20:15Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 135 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T04:20:17Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T04:20:17Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T04:20:17Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 04:20:17 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T04:20:21Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T04:20:21Z {T17.1} Argus: Refused to act on C1 - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T04:20:21Z {T18.1} Argus: Moved the incident to FIXING - no explanation left to try - no action was taken, and the evidence offers nothing further
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T04:21:37Z {T19.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/557
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T04:21:37Z {T20.1} Argus: Moved the incident to ESCALATED - a draft pull request is open at https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/557

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 03:43–04:12 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 48 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 31 {G46bc.2} minutes, 03:43–04:13 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 03:43–04:19 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 40.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 04:19 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 4 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 6 {Gad41.2} minutes, 04:03–04:08 {Gad41.3}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 134 {G971b.1} / on 66 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 04:13 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 13 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 04:13–04:19 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 04:14–04:19 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at about 04:13 {C1.1}. With it on, the account page's spend summary code hits a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to about 33% {C1.3}. No deployment, config change or rollout split is recorded, and the replicas did not move. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, never tried: the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person]

Actions it took:
  - none

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] average_spend_per_item_this_month divided total_this_month_cents by the number of purchases in the current month. That number is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, which is a common case. The test fixtures even call it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, this code never runs. As the flag rolled out to 100% {F1.1}, every such shopper's account page raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which is why the error rate rose step by step as the rollout progressed.
      
      The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the monthly average is 0 {F1.2} (the shopper spent nothing across zero items), and the function returns 0 {F1.3} without dividing. The return type stays int, so callers are unaffected. Nothing changes for shoppers who did buy this month. With the flag off, the page still shows the lifetime figure. The lifetime average still raises for an account with no purchases at all. That behaviour is deliberate and has its own test, so I left it alone. Errors are not swallowed: the only change is that the empty case is now handled explicitly. A regression test reproduces the incident's input through render_spend_summary with the flag on. On the current code that test raises ZeroDivisionError.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #557 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases they made this month without handling a shopper who bought nothing this month, so for any shopper who has bought before but not this month the page raises ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: A setting that shows shoppers their spending this month came on, and the code behind it likely fails when a shopper has bought nothing yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages returned errors.
still_at_risk: Account pages of shoppers who have not bought anything this month could keep failing while the monthly spend feature stays on, and the feature could come on again without any change showing in the flag provider's history.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors from the onset, and the account page error rate was at its highest at {Gbac1.7}. (cites Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; AL1)
causal_chain 2: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 during {G5309.3}. This error did not appear in the log lines before the onset. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The monthly-spend-feature flag was off for every evaluation during {G7e5d.4}. It was on for part of the evaluations at {G971b.6} (on {G971b.2}, off {G971b.1} of {G971b.3}) and on for every evaluation during {Gce95.4}. Neither the production change events read at {T9.1} nor the flag provider's history read at {T15.1} shows this change, so the record does not show what switched the flag. All replicas ran the same revision when read at {T10.1}, but the record does not show whether that revision was already running before the onset, so a change to it was not ruled out. (cites G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T9, under "What Argus did, in order"; T15, under "What Argus did, in order"; T10, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: The client-disconnect failures on account pages: they were logged well before the onset while the account page error rate stayed at its usual {Gbac1.6}, and they stopped at the onset. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: With the flag on, the account page runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month and fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: No check was seen that ran the spend summary with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on for shoppers.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The division failure would have been found before the flag reached any shopper, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors 2: The flag went from on for part of the evaluations to on for all of them by the next minute. No rollout stage was seen that held or reversed it as account page errors rose.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that stopped on the rising account page error rate would have kept the failures to a small share of shoppers and switched the flag back off.
contributing_factors 3: The flag coming on did not appear in the flag provider's history or in the production change events, so the change was not in the record of what changed.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: With the change recorded, Argus could have acted on C1 and turned the flag off, which would have ended the failures sooner instead of leaving it to a person.
contributing_factors 4: No on-call incident was linked to the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors 4 had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person could have turned the flag off once Argus left undoing it to a person, which would have shortened the incident.
action_items 1: Turn monthly-spend-feature off on io-shop until the fix in PR #557 is merged and deployed.
action_items 2: Before any feature flag on io-shop can be enabled in production, require tests that run the code behind the flag with the flag on, including the case of a shopper with no purchases in the current period.
action_items 3: Roll out flags such as monthly-spend-feature in stages that pause and switch the flag back off automatically when the account page error rate rises.
action_items 4: Find out how monthly-spend-feature came on with no change in the flag provider's history or in the production change events.
action_items 5: Make every change to io-shop feature flags go through the flag provider so that the change appears in its history.
action_items 6: Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
